newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's ruling party wins by-election.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's ruling party wins by-election.

text.p: Bangladesh's ruling Awami League candidate Ramesh Chandra Sen won a parliamentary by-election boycotted by the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), election commission officials said on Wednesday.
The commission said Sen polled 78,208 votes against 39,843 by his nearest rival, Z.H.N. Islam of the Jatiya Party headed by former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad.
The officials said the election in northern Thakurgaon was peaceful and 50.98 percent of voters cast ballots.
The seat fell vacant with the death of a ruling party member.

The BNP of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia and the fundamentalist Jamaat-e-Islami vowed not to participate in any polls as long as the chief election commissioner, Mohammad Abu Hena, held office.
Both parties accused Hena of favouring the Awami League in last year's general elections, although international observers said the polls were free and fair.
